text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service inference-proxy-canary (severity: P2) — incidentbot detected heartbeat jitter across canary probes in us-west/us-east-eu.

pagerduty-bot: PD#1045 — triggered on rule: canary-liveness-heartbeat-fuzzy-threshold. Link: https://pd.example/INC1045

alex.ng: acked (oncall). I'm looking.

maya.k: saw the spike on dashboards a sec ago — small amplitude 200-400ms spikes on proxy-accept latency, 3x in last 2m. No 5xxs.

samir: checking logs and canary runner. `kubectl -n infra logs canary-runner-5f7` shows repeated probe timeouts at approx 12:03:21.

alex.ng: running quick query: `sum(rate(proxy_request_latency_bucket[1m])) by (region)` — spikes primarily us-west.

maya.k: tagging PD: likely synthetic canary noise. No customer error reports yet. @oncall: do we want soft-suppress for 5m?

alex.ng: yes — applying soft suppression on PD for canary-liveness-heartbeat-fuzzy-threshold for 5m, note in PD that we're investigating.

pagerduty-bot: Suppression applied (user: alex.ng) — PD suppression ID sup-8723 — will auto-lift in 5m.

samir: confirmed canary runner restarted a minute ago (cron jitter), looking at runner logs: `restart reason: transient docker pull timeout` — retries caused probe blips.

maya.k: no regional traffic impact in telemetry. customer-facing latencies stable. marking no-impact.

alex.ng: posting quick mitigation in thread and closing loop: will bump canary runner backoff to reduce rapid restart flaps. Filing follow-up: #ticket INF-7203.

incident-bot: Alert auto-resolved (PD cleared) — condition returned to normal.

alex.ng: thanks — letting suppression lift. follow-up in INF-7203 includes runbook tweak and suppression tuning.

maya.k: adding note to runbook: if canary runner restarts within 1m of previous restart, auto-suppress PD and create followup.

samir: thumbs up. closing thread unless someone objects :thumbsup:
